welcome.label: Welcome · the cold cocoa cart

parts.label: 🌡️ Today
parts.title: How does heat move?
parts.body: Warm to cool, and which materials carry it fast or slow it down.

welcome.script:
(Wrap both hands around a warm mug.) Mmm. Where is this warmth going?

[ON SCREEN: The boat parade]
In Florida, December brings lighted boat parades. Rosa sells hot cocoa at the one in Palmetto Beach.

[ON SCREEN: The menu]
This year she switched to shiny metal mugs. Now the cocoa goes cold, and the handles get hot!

[ON SCREEN: Today]
Today you help Sam find out why. Read the menu and the order slips just below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · three spoons in a mug (Clue 1)
warmup.script:
(Hold up a metal spoon and a wooden spoon.) Two spoons. One cup of hot cocoa. Which handle would you rather hold?

[ON SCREEN: Three spoons]
Guess first. Then wait one minute and touch the spots up each handle. Watch your heat map fill in. If you have both spoons at home, try it for real with an adult and a warm drink. Press Listen on Sam’s walkie-talkie, right below me.

part1.label: Part 1 · be the heat (Clue 2)
part1.script:
(Hold an ice cube, or pretend to.) Brrr! Is the ice putting cold INTO my hand? Or is my hand losing something?

[ON SCREEN: Be the heat]
You be the heat. Drag the red dots and see which way they can go. Then try the Send cold button. Does it work? Press Listen.

part2.label: Part 2 · the butter rod race (Clue 3)
part2.script:
(Hold up a pencil like a rod and point to one end.) Heat goes in here. How fast does it get to the other end?

[ON SCREEN: The rod race]
Pick three rods, predict which butter dot falls off first, then heat the ends. Race a metal rod against one that isn’t metal.

explore.label: Part 3 · the Cup Race (Clue 4)

parts.label: 🧊 Ice on two blocks
parts.title: Which ice melts first?
parts.body: Touch, check with a thermometer, predict, then drop the ice.

explore.script:
(Hold up a foam cup and a metal cup.) Same warm water in both. Which one keeps it warm longer?

[ON SCREEN: The Cup Race]
Predict, then watch the graph. The higher the line, the warmer the water. Press Listen.

[ON SCREEN: Ice on two blocks]
Then don’t skip the ice blocks. The block that feels coldest might surprise you!

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: What went wrong at the cart?
parts.body: Pick the answer that fits all four clues.

parts.label: ☕ Rosa’s new mug
parts.title: Design and test it
parts.body: Mug, lid, handle. Run the parade test.

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
Four clues: why did Rosa’s cocoa go cold, and why did the handles get hot?

[ON SCREEN: Rosa’s new mug]
Then design Rosa a better mug and run the parade test.

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Last, two short answers, your conductor and insulator chart with a labeled sketch, and your CER.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “Cold flows out of ice cubes into my hand.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The claim]
Cold flows out of ice? Hmm. Think about those red heat dots, and that “Send cold” button.

There’s no wrong side, as long as you prove it.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Tap your side and two facts, then explain how they prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…” Press Listen.

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🧾 Your specimen
parts.title: Order slip #15
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: 🧥 Bonus
parts.title: The coat on the snow cone

parts.label: ➡ Next time
parts.title: Energy changes
parts.body: Sort the evidence: where did the energy start, and what did it become?

closing.script:
(Wrap your hands around the mug again.) Now you know where that warmth goes: from the mug into my hands.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist, and order slip number fifteen goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Bonus]
Want a surprise? Put a coat on a snow cone.

[ON SCREEN: Tool of the Week]
And try the infrared thermometer on this bench.

[ON SCREEN: Next time]
Next time: tracking energy as it changes!

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.
